rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralMatch`. They cover each obligation in its text. I reviewed the supplied test sources and did not request implementation source.

- **`new(node, excerpt)` constructor:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[callers_can_construct_complete_and_partial_search_results]` calls `StructuralMatch::new(address.clone(), "example".into())`. It then asserts that `node` equals the supplied `OutlineData` and `excerpt` equals "example". Because it is an integration test outside the crate, it also shows that `new` is the public way to construct the struct.
- **`node` identifies the enclosing outline item:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` runs real structural searches over Rust and Python files. It asserts that `node.path` and `node.selector` identify the enclosing item. For example, the match for `call()` has selector `fn[visible]` and path `visible.rs`, and the Python match has path `script.py`. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope]` asserts path `src/one.rs` and selector `fn[cached]`.
- **`excerpt` holds the matched range, which may be smaller than the enclosing item:** Both search tests assert that `excerpt` is exactly `call()`. The enclosing item is the whole `fn visible() { call(); }` or `fn[cached]`, so the tests show the excerpt is the matched range and not the whole item.
- **Struct shape and public fields:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against rustdoc and compiles the Habeas consumer against the SDK. The tests also read `node` and `excerpt` as public fields from outside the crate.
- **`#[non_exhaustive]`:** Nothing tests this attribute directly. It could only be checked with a compile-fail test, and I judged that outside what this requirement needs. The integration tests build the struct only through `new`, which is consistent with the attribute.

The text names no other boundary or failure case for this type, and no {fixme} acknowledgments apply.
